correctness.rationale: For all positive lengths, the exact 4x4 hat Gram matrix is symmetric positive definite and becomes an irreducible strictly diagonally dominant Stieltjes matrix after alternating-sign conjugation. The kernel absolute integral is convex on each element, so the norm is one of four signed row integrals. Exact rational identities show each endpoint row strictly dominates its neighboring interior row, the shorter terminal element determines the maximizing endpoint, and 5/3 < each endpoint row < 8/3. Strict positivity follows from explicit positive-coefficient polynomial certificates. The two exact degeneration limits prove sharpness without finite attainment; kernel sign inputs attain fixed-mesh norms. All symbolic identities and limits were independently reconstructed by bundled checker.py; finite quadrature samples supplement but do not replace the universal proof.

value.rationale: The first nontrivial fixed-resolution three-cell spline projector is a motivated stability benchmark for adaptive least-squares finite elements. Its exact 8/3 sharp upper constant improves the unrestricted dimension-one bound 3, the lower 5/3 bound is also sharp without finite attainment, and the unexpected shorter-terminal-cell localization gives a practical worst-error location. The two different mesh degenerations reveal precise changes under clustering rather than an arbitrary isolated parameter computation.
